prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton California?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick a single “best” personal injury lawyer for Pleasanton — the right attorney depends on the type of injury, how serious it is, whether you need a trial lawyer, and what style of communication and fee arrangement you prefer. I can, however, help you find the best one for your case. A quick plan:

1) Quick questions so I can narrow recommendations
- What type of case? (auto crash, slip & fall, dog bite, medical malpractice, wrongful death, workplace injury, etc.)
- When did it happen and how serious are your injuries?
- Do you want a Pleasanton‑based lawyer or is Alameda/Contra Costa/Santa Clara OK?
- Do you prefer a lawyer who will litigate (go to trial) or one focused on settlements?
- Any language or scheduling preferences?

2) Where to look for highly rated personal injury attorneys
- California State Bar attorney search (to confirm license and discipline record)
- Super Lawyers (lists recognized lawyers by region)
- Avvo and Martindale‑Hubbell (peer and client reviews, ratings)
- Google/Yelp reviews and local Facebook community groups
- Referrals from your primary care doctor, friends, or other attorneys

3) Key qualifications and signals of a good PI lawyer
- Substantial experience handling cases like yours (same injury type)
- Trial experience and willingness to go to court if necessary
- Strong track record of settlements/verdicts (ask for examples)
- Clear contingency fee agreement (typical range ~33%–40% plus costs; confirm specifics)
- Good client communication and timely responses
- Solid client reviews and no serious disciplinary history

4) Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?
- What is your approach to settlement vs. trial?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (partner, associate, paralegal)?
- What is your fee and how are expenses handled?
- How long do you expect my case to take?
- Can you provide references from past clients?

5) Red flags
- Pressure to sign immediately
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or outcome
- Poor communication during the initial contact
- No written fee agreement

If you want, tell me the type and details of your injury and whether you prefer a Pleasanton office, and I’ll (a) suggest a short list of well‑matched firms to consider and (b) draft a short script/email you can use to contact them for consultations. Which would you like?
